name: clinical_v0_graph_redirect_half
rationale: Composed final-layer weights identify units 198 and 38 as positive readout paths that activate for high normalized values. In 128 calibration patients, their active cases remain underestimated after the original affine correction; almost all are measured variables rather than static/administrative channels. Increase only these two effective output coefficients by 1%, a fixed conservative expansion of the existing learned paths. Negative GELU-tail contributions change in the opposite direction, also consistent with the common positive offset in the low/middle range. No fitting, gradients, optimizer or test data. Exact median-draw activations of the edited model show unit 198 still underestimating in its positive intermediate range (median normalized errors -0.0128, -0.0327, -0.0492 in activation bins 0-0.5, 0.5-1, 1-2), across 93, 81, 96 calibration patients. Above 2 the median error reverses sign to +0.0223. Add a localized triangular correction in preactivation z198: k*(GELU(16*z)-4*GELU(16*(z-1.5))+3*GELU(16*(z-2)))/16, k=0.04*the current effective coefficient. It rises toward the strongest intermediate underestimation and switches off before the high tail. A single fixed 4% slope is used; no fitting or sweep. Reuse three existing neurons with negligible effective contributions. Unit 38 is unchanged because its remaining residual signs are inconsistent. The running benchmark candidate remains unchanged; no clinical test result informed this proposal. Compose the independent 1% sharpening of negative-only head unit 47, using its already specified weights unchanged. The local positive repair reduced mean confirmation MSE but cost MAE; unit 47 sharpening reduced MAE on both confirmation seeds but slightly cost MSE. They address intermediate underestimation and a common positive negative-tail contribution through disjoint neurons. No coefficient is refitted, searched or derived from test. Test their composition as a single new hypothesis, retaining it only if full forward evaluations support joint improvement. New calibration median-draw preactivations show unit 255 remains entirely negative. Its negative coefficient turns GELU's negative lobe into a positive output hump. For z in [-1.5,-1), residual median is +0.00673; for z in [-1,-0.5), it is -0.00197, each across 127 patients. Translate this hump by changing only incoming bias 255 by -0.01. This lowers its left-tail contribution and raises its contribution near zero, unlike uniform attenuation. The pattern is stronger on static/admin/time variables; physiological subgroup signs are mixed. This is one fixed hypothesis on an experimental parent, not a demonstrated causal correction. No gradients, training, parameter sweep or test residuals are used. V1 test scores have already been seen in the ongoing benchmark; any later test is a repeated benchmark assessment. The two positive head paths 38 and 198 have partly aligned incoming weights (cosine 0.69). Normally z38 is below z198. A positive contrast z38-z198 occurs in only 15 median-selected scoring entries across 11 of 512 calibration patients in the gate255 model; its median and mean normalized residuals are negative. Six cases overpredict, so the association is neither universal nor causal proof. An enriched target-free probe shows this contrast remains sparse at both noise steps. Reuse nearly disconnected units 181 and 150 to implement a small capped ramp: A*(GELU(64*d)-GELU(64*(d-1)))/64, d=z38-z198, A=0.05*effective_coefficient38. The zero threshold detects order reversal, the unit contrast caps the response, and the fixed 5% amplitude is not fitted to residual magnitudes. Sharpness confines the small negative GELU lobe near the threshold. No derivatives, training, optimizer, coefficient sweep or test targets are used. This is a new hypothesis requiring complete forward evaluations. A separate structural hypothesis concerns the only AdaptiveGCN in this clinical model. Its adaptive factors are ordinary tensors in a Python support list: absent from both the released state_dict and model.parameters. The inference harness reconstructs and freezes them, but their variable relations are not learned checkpoint parameters. The saved clinical adjacency is symmetric and its normalized forward/backward supports are identical. Move a fixed half of each adaptive graph-power channel matrix to the corresponding saved supports, dividing it equally between the two existing paths. Retain the other half on the original adaptive branch. Every support is row stochastic; therefore the sum of channel matrices, and the response to features constant across variables, are preserved in real arithmetic. Float32 rounding is verified separately. This edits only one saved convolution tensor and retains the original runtime layout, all graph factors, and all V4 head changes. Half is a fixed structural midpoint, not a fitted coefficient or part of a sweep. This may still harm a network adapted to the original mixing, so require both MAE and MSE to improve in the complete paired forward. No targets, residuals, gradients, optimizer, training or metric-driven fitting are used to construct this hypothesis. No claim that the saved graph is necessarily superior.
